science: Shadow formation, rectilinear propagation of light, umbra and penumbra from an extended source: any school optics text.

Shadow size from similar triangles: shadow height is about object height times the light-to-wall distance divided by the light-to-object distance. The numbers in e1 are worked out this way for an 8 centimetre toy, a torch on the table 1 metre from the wall, and the toy 15, 50 and 70 centimetres from the wall.

Mohist Canon optics entries on shadows (two lights give two shadows, shadow size depends on slant and distance, the shadow does not move but is re-formed): Joseph Needham, Science and Civilisation in China, volume 4 part 1 (1962), and A. C. Graham, Later Mohist Logic, Ethics and Science (1978).
Shade avoidance in plants, sensed through the red to far-red ratio by phytochromes: standard plant biology, for example Casal, Annual Review of Plant Biology (2013).
Black heron (Egretta ardesiaca) canopy feeding, with its purpose debated: standard ornithology accounts.
Giant clams retract their mantle in response to shadows, using many small eyes along the mantle edge.
Lotte Reiniger, Die Abenteuer des Prinzen Achmed (1926), the oldest surviving animated feature film.

Lunar and solar eclipses as shadows of the Earth and the Moon.

roots.context: We have made shadows grow, shrink, split in two and tell a story. Now we ask what the Near or Far test tells us about shadows, and about ourselves.

deep_truth.truth: Your toy stayed the same size, yet its shadow grew as you moved it nearer the torch. A shadow is the patch the toy keeps light from reaching. Near the torch, the toy blocks a wider spread of the light. So a shadow's size is set by where the toy stands, as much as by the toy.
deep_truth.habit: We think of a shadow as a dark copy that belongs to a thing, with the thing's own size. But the same toy made a small shadow and a huge one. The size came from the toy's place between the light and the wall.
deep_truth.evidence: In the Near or Far test, the toy's shadow was only a little taller than the toy near the wall, and about three times as tall near the torch. The toy did not change at all.

three.who_am_i: You are something light cannot pass through. Wherever you stand in the light, you leave a patch of shade behind you.
three.what_is_life: A plant feels the shade of a neighbour and grows taller to reach the light. Living beings sense shadows and act on them.
three.what_is_this_world: The world is full of light and of the shapes that block it. Night itself is your side of the Earth in the Earth's own shadow.

roots.thread: One torch and one toy made a small sharp shadow, a big fuzzy one, and, with a second torch, two pale shadows. The toy never changed. Each shadow was a different meeting of the same light with the same toy. A shadow is made by the light, the thing and the surface together, and by where each one is.

teachings.teaching: The Katha Upanishad speaks of two that live together in the body. It says the wise call them shadow and sunlight.
teachings.link: In your tests, a shadow was only ever there because of the light. Shadow and light come as a pair: switch off the torch, and the shadow goes too.

teachings.teaching: The Tao Te Ching, an old Chinese book, says that long and short show each other, and high and low lean on each other.
teachings.link: Your toy's shadow was not long or short by itself. It was long or short depending on where the toy stood between the torch and the wall.

teachings.teaching: Plato, a Greek thinker, told of people who could see only shadows on a cave wall, and thought the shadows were the real things.
teachings.link: A shadow shows an outline, but not the colour or the true size. In the Near or Far test, a small toy made a giant shadow. You knew the toy, so the shadow could not fool you.

science.text: Light travels in straight lines through air, so a shadow has the outline of the thing that blocks the light.
Plants sense the shade of other leaves with light-sensing proteins called phytochromes, and grow longer stems to reach the light.

other_view.view: Some philosophers say a shadow is only a place where light is missing, so it is not anything at all. They say its 'size' is only a way of talking about where the light is.

practice.title: Breathing Shadow
practice.say: Sit near a wall with the torch on. Hold one hand up in the light, so its shadow is on the wall. Breathe in slowly, and move your hand towards the torch. Watch the shadow grow. Breathe out slowly, and move your hand back to the wall. Watch it shrink. Do this five times. Your hand stayed the same. What changed?
practice.kid: Hold your hand in the torch light. Breathe in, and move it to the torch. Watch the shadow grow. Breathe out, and move it back. Watch it shrink. Do it five times.

ask: If a shadow is only missing light, why can we still measure it?
Your shadow is a different size under every light. Which one is really yours?
When you stand in a grown-up's shadow, you make no shadow of your own. Where has your shadow gone?

how_we_found_out.story: Long ago, in many lands, people thought a shadow was a part of a person, like a dark copy that followed them. Some thought it was even a part of their soul. About 2,300 years ago in China, the followers of a thinker called Mozi watched shadows closely. They are called the Mohists. They wrote short notes about light, in a book now called the Mohist Canon. One note says that two lights make two shadows. Another says that the size of a shadow changes with how far the thing is from the light. A third says that a shadow does not really move. Where the light comes back, the old shadow is gone, and a new one forms in the new place. These notes fit a simpler idea than a dark copy. A shadow is the place where a thing blocks the light. A copy of you would not double, grow or vanish. You can check each of the Mohists' notes yourself, with a torch and a toy.
how_we_found_out.who: The Mohists, followers of the thinker Mozi in China
how_we_found_out.when: About 2,300 years ago (the 4th to 3rd centuries BCE)
how_we_found_out.wrong_idea: That a shadow is a dark copy of a person, or even part of their soul, that follows them about. Watching how shadows double under two lights, and grow and shrink with distance, showed that a shadow is only where light is blocked.
